function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "The move_to tool only executed a full segment on the very first call (39 steps, 1.9s); every later call, regardless of direction (x, y, z, diagonal) or of letting the arm settle, returned after about 0.1s and moved the end-effector only 1-4 mm (e.g., commanded z=0.90 repeatedly, never got below z=0.970). With 8 calls left I cannot descend the remaining ~4 cm to the block (block top near z=0.845), fix a ~3 cm lateral offset of the block from the finger-pad centerline, grasp, lift, and carry it to the bowl; the required ~25 cm of travel plus the grasp is far beyond the ~2-4 mm per call the tool is delivering, so the task cannot be completed within the remaining budget.", "hindsight": "Rig facts learned this trial: (1) The tool layer truncated nearly every motion to a ~0.1s / 1-3 control-step segment: only the first command of the trial (from the fully settled initial state) ran a full 39-step 1.9s segment; after that all commands moved the eef only 1-4 mm, so large Cartesian moves (descents to z=0.90, lateral corrections) never completed and repeated subtargets were needed. Plan assuming ~1-4 mm of eef motion per call, and check the measured eef each observation rather than trusting targets. (2) At the start pose (eef x=-0.11, z=1.0) a +6 cm x command moved the eef +4.7 cm; the same direction later stalled, so motion feasibility was configuration dependent. (3) Wrist view geometry: the two finger pads are the gray prongs at the bottom corners of the frame (midline ~0.51 image width); the red block sat ~3 cm right of that midline and a few cm below the pad level when the eef was at z~0.97, i.e., the gripper was still ~3-4 cm above grasp height; the blue bowl appeared farther up-image beyond the block (beyond it along the approach direction). (4) The front camera horizontal axis did not follow x motion; the side camera shows the bowl offset laterally ~14 cm from the block. (5) Open gripper measures ~0.99; the trial started at 0.52 (intermediate)."}
